  "text": "My sister arrived with a tin of buttons and the coat I had left at our mother's house.

“You're missing one,” she said.

“I know.”

“For three years?”

She laid the coat across my knees. The empty thread loops were still there, below the collar.

We tipped the buttons onto a tea towel. There were brass ones, wooden ones, small white ones joined by lengths of cotton.

“She never threw anything away,” I said.

“She threw plenty away. Just not useful things.”

My sister found a brown button and held it against the coat.

“Too big.”

“It would stay shut.”

“So would a padlock.”

She smiled and put it back.

At the bottom of the tin was a blue button shaped like a flower. I remembered it on a cardigan she had worn to school.

“You hated that,” I said.

“You told everyone it was baby clothes.”

“I was nine.”

“I was six.”

She took it from me and slipped it into her pocket.

We found a match eventually, almost black, with a chipped rim. She threaded the needle while I fetched scissors.

“I can do it,” I said.

“I've started now.”

I stood beside her while she sewed. She used doubled thread, then wound it beneath the button, making a little stalk the way our mother had.

When she finished, I put the coat on.

“Turn round.”

“It's a button.”

“Let me see.”

I turned.

She straightened the collar, then took her hands away.

“That's better.”

We gathered the spare buttons. Under the table, I found one neither of us had noticed, and gave it to her."
